subject: Cloud marketplace selection, timing & who signs: recommendation for MedStream pilot
messages:

Subject: Procurement path for pilot — marketplace or direct?

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked good for our clinical summarization pilot. Procurement asked me to clarify one thing before we move to a PO: should we buy through the cloud marketplace (Azure/GCP) or execute a direct contract/PO with Redwood? Their specific questions:

- Which route gets us an invoice addressed to MedStream (we need it for a PO & cost center)?
- If we buy via marketplace, who is the seller of record and how does that affect refunds/credits?
- Does co-sell eligibility or partner discounts change the recommended lane?
- Rough timing: which path is faster for a small pilot (3 months, <$50k)?

We have an internal deadline to issue a PO by end of month — appreciate a short recommendation and any worksheets we can pass to procurement.

Best,
Hannah

Head of Partnerships, MedStream Health

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah@medstream.health>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement path for pilot — marketplace or direct?

Hannah — good questions, thanks. Long story short: for a short pilot where procurement needs a standard PO + predictable invoicing, we usually recommend a private offer / direct invoice path over a public marketplace listing. Quick rationale below plus the practical tradeoffs for Azure/GCP: 

1) Invoice & PO mapping: the private offer (or direct invoice) route lets MedStream be buyer-of-record on our invoice, so your AP team can map the vendor and cost center cleanly. Public marketplace purchases often route invoicing through the cloud provider and may show the provider as seller of record — that complicates refunds and PO reconciliation.

2) Timing: marketplace can be fast if you use credit card/self-serve. But for an enterprise PO, private offer + DocuSign MSA can be completed in ~5-10 business days once terms are agreed, whereas marketplace private offers (partner-managed) sometimes add another 3–7 business days for provider review. For a $50k pilot, private offer is usually the fastest path to an enterprise-style PO.

3) Seller of record & refunds:
   - Azure/GCP marketplace (public): provider often shows as seller of record. Refunds/credits flow through them, which adds an extra ticketing hop.
   - Private offer/direct invoice: Redwood remains seller of record — we handle credits/refunds directly and can apply retroactive credits to closed invoices if needed.

4) Co-sell and partner incentives: if MedStream plans to expand later and wants co-sell credits to the partner/reseller, listing on marketplace can enable certain partner incentives, especially on Azure. But co-sell qualification is separate from procurement path and often requires additional registration steps; it should not block the pilot PO.

5) Compliance & data residency: if you need specific invoice residency or legal language in the MSA, direct routes are easier to surface custom clauses.

Attached is a quick matrix (Marketplace_vs_PrivateOffer_matrix.xlsx) and an MSA highlights PDF you can share with procurement. If helpful, I recommend: choose private offer/direct invoice for this pilot to keep the AP workflow simple, then evaluate marketplace listing when you move to production.

Next step: if you want to go private offer, we can send the private-offer worksheet and a DocuSign MSA for signatures.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Marketplace_vs_PrivateOffer_matrix.xlsx]

Alex — happy to own vendor info and next steps. Short answers:

- Yes, we will provide Redwood's W-9 / tax ID and the remit-to address on the private-offer invoice. I'll attach the standard remit block in the worksheet.
- If you later migrate to an Azure or GCP marketplace purchase, Redwood can still issue invoice-level credits for product refunds or billing adjustments, but the timing/process changes: provider reconciliation windows can introduce 30–60 day delays for adjustments. We recommend keeping an internal tag on the contract so your finance team knows to expect potential lag.

What I'll send now: the Azure_Private_Offer_worksheet.xlsx (pre-filled with Redwood remit address), a short MSA highlights PDF (MedStream_MSA_highlights.pdf), and a DocuSign link template. Estimated turnaround: once we get the signed PO + MSA, we can issue the private offer and be invoicing within 2 business days.

Action items:

- Hannah: confirm you want the DocuSign MSA sent to your signer (name/email).

Thanks — Lauren
